headline: Youth killed by 'Indian Khasis' at Sylhet border
summary: 25-year-old Minhaj Uddin was shot while collecting betel nuts from the Meghalaya region of India.
details: A 25-year-old man named Minhaj Uddin, a resident of Bhadeshwar village in Gowainghat, Sylhet, was killed after being shot in the Lakhate area of Meghalaya, India.
The incident occurred around 3:00 AM on Friday. Minhaj died on Saturday morning around 7:00 AM while being transported to a hospital.

According to local sources, Minhaj and several others had entered India to collect betel nuts. While they were in the Lakhate station area, 'Indian Khasis' opened fire on them, leaving Minhaj wounded.
His companions rescued him and brought him back to the Bangladesh border. Lieutenant Colonel Md. Nazmul Haque, commander of the 48 BGB battalion in Sylhet, confirmed the incident.
Minhaj was the primary breadwinner for his family, supporting an elderly father and an ill older brother. He was involved in the betel nut trade.
The body has been sent to Sylhet MAG Osmani Medical College Hospital for an autopsy to determine the exact cause of death, according to Gowainghat Police Station OC Omar Faruq.
caption:

His companions rescued him and brought him back to the Bangladesh border. Lieutenant Colonel Md. Nazmul Haque, commander of the 48 BGB battalion in Sylhet, confirmed the incident.

Minhaj was the primary breadwinner for his family, supporting an elderly father and an ill older brother. He was involved in the betel nut trade.

The body has been sent to Sylhet MAG Osmani Medical College Hospital for an autopsy to determine the exact cause of death, according to Gowainghat Police Station OC Omar Faruq.

headline: Loss of 4 Taka per egg: Poultry farmers face massive losses
summary: Farmers claim production costs are 10 Taka per egg while selling prices are only 6 Taka, leading to a monthly loss of 500 crore Taka.
details: The Bangladesh Poultry Industries Association (BPIA) has raised alarms over the severe financial crisis facing poultry farmers. They claim that while the production cost of a single egg is 10 Taka, the selling price at the farm level is only 6 Taka.
caption:
Production cost: 10 Taka. Selling price: 6 Taka. Poultry farmers are losing 4 Taka on every single egg they produce.
